rv.q: Holland and iLongwe are the title figures, Ogun Size and younger brother Oshoosi Size; Mays is Elegba, just out of prison, along with Oshoosi, and looking for more trouble than Oshoosi is now that they’re released on probation.
The minimal scenery is a circle of salt (or sand, or both) that the actors make, then come in and out of to denote their presence in any given scene, a not-so-Caucasian Chalk Circle, if you will.

Otis Redding’s “Try a Little Tenderness” features prominently in Tarell Alvin McCraney’s The Brothers Size, and for good reason. The play, which I first saw in 2009 as the middle section of McCraney’s remarkable trilogy The Brother/Sister Plays, spins out ideas of roughness and tenderness in the lives of young Black men in 21st-century America.
